title: Signature Milk and Honey Rice Porridge Replica
closeness_reason: Cooked rice in sweetened milk is the original dish itself, rebuilt on a milk and honey base, so flavour, texture, and appearance all match closely.
description: Signature original design. Rice porridge is short-grain rice simmered slowly in milk until the grains soften and release starch, thickening the milk into a creamy spoonable dish, then sweetened with honey. This replica uses the milk and honey base as its defining ingredients: whole milk for body, rice for starch, and honey stirred in at the end so its aroma survives the cooking. It is the simplest grain replica in this pair because it needs only one pan, gentle heat, and patience, and it teaches the core grain lesson that starch, given time and liquid, thickens on its own.
original_food: Rice porridge cooked in milk and sweetened with honey, the warm breakfast dish served thick from the pan.

ingredients: Ground cinnamon or vanilla, to serve
method: Combine the rice, milk, and salt in a heavy pan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often so the rice does not catch, and cook for 35 to 40 minutes until the rice is soft and the mixture is thick and creamy.
Remove from the heat and stir in the honey until dissolved.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm with cinnamon or vanilla.
instructions: Combine the rice, milk, and salt in a heavy pan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often so the rice does not catch, and cook for 35 to 40 minutes until the rice is soft and the mixture is thick and creamy.
Remove from the heat and stir in the honey until dissolved.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm with cinnamon or vanilla.
science: Rice porridge thickens by starch swelling: rice starch granules absorb hot milk, swell, and release starch chains that tangle and trap liquid, so the dish turns creamy without any added thickener. Milk fat and protein round out the texture and carry flavour, while honey added off the heat keeps its volatile aroma compounds that boiling would drive off. Gentle, frequent stirring prevents the starch from settling and scorching on the pan base.
safety: Use pasteurized milk and serve the porridge hot or promptly chilled. Use pasteurized milk. Milk is a major allergen; note lactose for anyone who avoids it. Honey is not for infants under 12 months (botulism risk).
storage: Store covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days; stir in a splash of milk when reheating, since the porridge thickens as it cools.
variations: Baked rice porridge: transfer to a buttered dish and bake at 160 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes for a golden top.
